currentContext.expansion: The annual report discloses no plant construction, capacity addition or commissioning project. Expansion in FY 2025-26 is footprint and channel led. The Distribution Centre was shifted from Serampore to Panpur, stated to reduce rent, logistic and other cost, and the Company upgraded its logistics network with new transport options to ensure more timely deliveries. To optimise capacity utilisation in the distribution division the Company expanded its range of PU and EVA products, improved design and quality and rationalised pricing, and implemented TOC-based stock management to reduce overall inventory alongside merchandising, design and value engineering. As on March 31, 2026 the distribution footprint was a network of 791 distributors across India, with strong emphasis in the eastern region. Looking forward, the Company states it is focusing on product innovation and demand traction to improve margins with the expansion of distribution points to deepen its reach beyond Tier I - III cities, and is diversifying its product portfolio by revamping sandals, sports shoes, formal shoes and PU sandals. Provenance note: the Panpur site is a factory of the Company and became its Registered Office with effect from December 10, 2025 (shifted from Flat No. 4A, Kalyani Complex, Bangur Avenue, Kolkata) — this fact is stated in the Board's Report as supplied in the sibling profile and risks_esg bundles, not in the Directors' Report excerpt routed here. No commissioning timeline, no capacity number and no rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the routed text.

risks.note: Company-stated: demand may be affected by changing consumer preferences, seasonal trends and macroeconomic conditions. Mitigated through a diversified product portfolio, regular product introductions and an extensive distribution network catering to multiple customer segments. Management separately reports muted consumer demand and continued pressure on discretionary spending, particularly in the mass and value segments, which is exactly where this company sells.

Company-stated: fluctuations in the prices of key raw materials may impact profitability. Mitigated through strategic sourcing, supplier diversification, raw material import price optimisation and cost optimisation initiatives. Sharpened by the Company's own disclosure that at the fag end of FY 2025-26 the gulf conflict has set in uncertainties as to sourcing and pricing of petroleum based raw materials, and that input cost increase from the prolonged global conflict has carried over to FY 2026-27 till date — material for a portfolio built on EVA, PVC, PVC DIP and PU.

Company-stated: dependence on an extensive distributor network may affect market reach and product availability. Mitigated by strengthening channel relationships, enhancing distributor engagement and improving supply chain efficiencies. Structurally load-bearing because the entire business is wholesale distribution through 791 distributors selling into multi-brand outlets, with no owned retail channel described.

Company-stated: intense competition from organised and unorganised players may exert pressure on pricing and market share. Mitigated through product quality, competitive pricing, product innovation and brand visibility.

Company-stated: disruptions in manufacturing, logistics or the supply chain may impact business continuity. Mitigated through established operational processes, a diversified vendor base and continuous monitoring of supply chain performance.

Company-stated: changes in statutory, taxation and regulatory requirements may impact operations. Mitigated by internal processes to monitor regulatory developments and ensure timely compliance. Amplified in the near term because the Listing Regulations became applicable to the Company only from its listing date of 27th November 2025, so its listed-company compliance framework is in its first part-year.

Structural concentration disclosed but not labelled a risk by the Company: it states it is primarily engaged in one business segment, namely Footwear, with a distributor network across India carrying strong emphasis in the eastern region. There is no export, no second segment and no geographic hedge described anywhere in the routed text.

Neither the licence term, renewal conditions nor termination consequences are disclosed in the routed text.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India is described as a consumption led economy where increasing aspirations and affordability will continue to drive consumption; stated drivers are favourable demographics, steady growth in both rural and urban areas, increase in purchasing power, a growing young and working population, and increasing penetration of mobile technology and internet infrastructure altering consumer behaviour.
- The Indian footwear market is cited at USD 20.67 billion in 2025 and projected to reach USD 47.53 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 9.7% during 2026-2034 (third-party source cited by the Company).
- The global footwear market is cited at USD 476.8 billion in 2025, projected to grow from USD 496.2 billion in 2026 to USD 675.6 billion by 2033, a CAGR of 4.5% from 2026 to 2033 (third-party source cited by the Company).
- Policy support through the Indian Footwear and Leather Development Programme (IFLDP) is expected to enhance manufacturing capabilities, facilitate technology adoption, improve skill development and strengthen export competitiveness.
- Headwind: FY 2025-26 continued to be a challenging year for the footwear industry, with input cost increase due to prolonged global conflict (stated as carried over to FY 2026-27 till date), muted consumer demand and continued pressure on discretionary spending, particularly in the mass and value segments.
- Headwind: at the fag end of FY 2025-26 the gulf conflict has set in uncertainties as to sourcing and pricing of petroleum based raw materials.
- Mixed demand read: urban markets demonstrated pockets of resilience during the festive period, but overall consumption trends remained measured.
- Recovery expectation: the Indian economy is expected to see a gradual recovery in coming years, with growing consumer incomes and supportive government policies cited as fuelling this optimistic forecast.
- Structural demand drivers named for the industry: increasing population and urbanization, health awareness lifting athletic and sports shoes, fashion trends driving style and design, and comfort and customization as growth determinants.

- Governance of conduct — POSH: the Company has adopted a gender-neutral Prevention of Sexual Harassment policy covering permanent, contractual and temporary employees and management trainees, with an Internal Complaint Committee constituted. Complaints of sexual harassment received in the year: Nil (stated). Complaints disposed off during the year: N.A. (stated as not applicable, i.e. unknown/not populated rather than zero). Cases pending more than ninety days: N.A. The Company also states compliance with the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 for the year under review. [Provenance: back-filled from the Board's Report as supplied in the sibling strategy_outlook bundle; note that 'Nil' complaints received is a STATED NIL whereas the two 'N.A.' cells are unknown/not-applicable and must not be read as zero.]
- Governance of conduct — whistle-blower: a Vigil Mechanism / Whistle Blower policy is in place for employees and directors to report concerns about unethical practice, and no person has been denied access to the Chairperson of the Audit Committee. Board-adopted policies also include the Nomination and Remuneration Policy, a Policy on determination and disclosure of Materiality of Events or Information, a Policy on Materiality of Related Party Transactions and a Policy for determining Material Subsidiaries. [Provenance: the vigil-mechanism paragraph is back-filled from the Board's Report as supplied in the sibling capex_expansion bundle; the Board-adopted policy list is from the Corporate Governance report as supplied in the sibling governance_entities bundle. Note the mismatch: a 'Policy for determining Material Subsidiaries' has been adopted although the Company states it has no subsidiary, associate or joint venture.]
- Assurance: the Statutory Auditors and Secretarial Auditors reported no incident of fraud under Section 143(12) during the year, and neither the Auditors' Report nor the Secretarial Audit Report contains any qualification, reservation, adverse remark or disclaimer. Two of six directors are women (Mrs. Dhritipriya Raydasgupta and Mrs. Suman Murarka), both Independent, and the Audit Committee is chaired by a woman Independent Director. capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The annual report discloses no plant construction, capacity addition or commissioning project. Expansion in FY 2025-26 is footprint and channel led. The Distribution Centre was shifted from Serampore to Panpur, stated to reduce rent, logistic and other cost, and the Company upgraded its logistics network with new transport options to ensure more timely deliveries. To optimise capacity utilisation in the distribution division the Company expanded its range of PU and EVA products, improved design and quality and rationalised pricing, and implemented TOC-based stock management to reduce overall inventory alongside merchandising, design and value engineering. As on March 31, 2026 the distribution footprint was a network of 791 distributors across India, with strong emphasis in the eastern region. Looking forward, the Company states it is focusing on product innovation and demand traction to improve margins with the expansion of distribution points to deepen its reach beyond Tier I - III cities, and is diversifying its product portfolio by revamping sandals, sports shoes, formal shoes and PU sandals. Provenance note: the Panpur site is a factory of the Company and became its Registered Office with effect from December 10, 2025 (shifted from Flat No. 4A, Kalyani Complex, Bangur Avenue, Kolkata) — this fact is stated in the Board's Report as supplied in the sibling profile and risks_esg bundles, not in the Directors' Report excerpt routed here. No commissioning timeline, no capacity number and no rupee capex quantum is stated anywhere in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Distribution reach: a network of 791 distributors across India as on March 31, 2026, with strong emphasis in the eastern region, described as the lever for market reach and product availability.
- Brand access without brand ownership: a License Agreement with Khadim India Limited to use the well-established Khadim brand and specified sub-brands (Kalypso, Wash n' Wear, Fliers, FitNxt, Dunford, Pugo), each stated to have a targeted end user enabling broad market coverage.
- Integrated value chain: the business model spans product design, sourcing, manufacturing, quality assurance and wholesale distribution, stated to enable efficient execution across the value chain.
- Scalable, capital-light front end: the Distribution business is described as a highly scalable model on the front-end with a mix of in-house and contract manufacturing.
- Inherited operating base: as the resulting company of the Khadim India Limited demerger, it carries an established industry presence and extensive product expertise from its first year as an independent entity.
- Price-point coverage in the mass segment, with trendy products stated to range from Rs 75 to Rs 999.

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Demand Risk — Company-stated: demand may be affected by changing consumer preferences, seasonal trends and macroeconomic conditions. Mitigated through a diversified product portfolio, regular product introductions and an extensive distribution network catering to multiple customer segments. Management separately reports muted consumer demand and continued pressure on discretionary spending, particularly in the mass and value segments, which is exactly where this company sells.
- Raw Material Price Risk — Company-stated: fluctuations in the prices of key raw materials may impact profitability. Mitigated through strategic sourcing, supplier diversification, raw material import price optimisation and cost optimisation initiatives. Sharpened by the Company's own disclosure that at the fag end of FY 2025-26 the gulf conflict has set in uncertainties as to sourcing and pricing of petroleum based raw materials, and that input cost increase from the prolonged global conflict has carried over to FY 2026-27 till date — material for a portfolio built on EVA, PVC, PVC DIP and PU.
- Distribution Risk — Company-stated: dependence on an extensive distributor network may affect market reach and product availability. Mitigated by strengthening channel relationships, enhancing distributor engagement and improving supply chain efficiencies. Structurally load-bearing because the entire business is wholesale distribution through 791 distributors selling into multi-brand outlets, with no owned retail channel described.
- Competitive Risk — Company-stated: intense competition from organised and unorganised players may exert pressure on pricing and market share. Mitigated through product quality, competitive pricing, product innovation and brand visibility.
- Operational Risk — Company-stated: disruptions in manufacturing, logistics or the supply chain may impact business continuity. Mitigated through established operational processes, a diversified vendor base and continuous monitoring of supply chain performance.
- Regulatory & Compliance Risk — Company-stated: changes in statutory, taxation and regulatory requirements may impact operations. Mitigated by internal processes to monitor regulatory developments and ensure timely compliance. Amplified in the near term because the Listing Regulations became applicable to the Company only from its listing date of 27th November 2025, so its listed-company compliance framework is in its first part-year.
- Single-segment and single-geography concentration — Structural concentration disclosed but not labelled a risk by the Company: it states it is primarily engaged in one business segment, namely Footwear, with a distributor network across India carrying strong emphasis in the eastern region. There is no export, no second segment and no geographic hedge described anywhere in the routed text.
- Dependence on a licensed brand owned by a related party — Structural dependency disclosed but not labelled a risk by the Company: KSR sells entirely under the Khadim brand and its sub-brands (Kalypso, Wash n' Wear, Fliers, FitNxt, Dunford, Pugo) under a License Agreement with Khadim India Limited — an entity over which the Company's KMP and their relatives exercise significant influence, and which is also a counterparty for royalty, purchase of goods, sale of goods, shared services, rent and capital goods. Neither the licence term, renewal conditions nor termination consequences are disclosed in the routed text.
